properties.name: The fifteen 2026-10-30 fold and removal candidates are counted refusing stubs; each fold's survivor carries the job
properties.rationale:
Anthony 2026-10-30, "Yes, go with B" on dec:idea-make-the-tool-changes-now-after-a-snapshot-and-restore-what-is-missed-in-december, for req:the-2026-10-30-fold-and-removal-candidates-ship-as-counted-refusing-stubs-then-december-decides (the candidates of dec:idea-fold-and-removal-candidates-from-the-2026-10-30-counts; the amended dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first). Absence is silent, so a listed stub turns "it was missed" into a count; the re-count (about 2026-12-23, deprecation::RE_COUNT) deletes a stub nobody called and restores one somebody called. Choices made here, each to keep the count honest: the existing retirement registry is reused (one more entry kind, not a second mechanism); served text and find_tools never point at a stub, so the count measures need, not our own pointing; stub descriptions stay the tools' own in the router so no other tool's ranking moves (an earlier version that rewrote them shifted word weights and broke the rank ratchet); the remote client stopped answering unmeasurable set_artifact_checksum calls locally, which would have kept them out of the server's ledger. Ratchets: eight mutual pairs entered the baseline because a stub ranked above each left the top 5 (scores unchanged, shown with tools/tool_confusability.py against main's toolsnaps); the relation-share ceiling was re-measured, not loosened (the same 89 non-stub queries carry relations on main 4bc0811d5 and here; the 15 stub queries left the denominator); add_requirement now ranks first and left not_first. The surface record carries owner_approved_stubs with this approval named. The flo2 gateway calls set_artifact_checksum in files-api.ts and refuses it at the engine door: both go in the flo2 move PR after the release (the files-api change works on 0.95.0, so it can land first).
Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Fifteen tools stay listed and callable as counted refusing stubs (deprecation::REGISTRY Deprecation::stub, mark "RETIRED on 2026-10-30 (0.96.0) ...", handler service::stub_answer): each changes nothing, refuses with the call that does its job (a fold's refusal carries the exact survivor call built from the caller's arguments), is read-only, and is written to the usage ledger under its own name; usage_report gains retired_stubs (each stub's count in the window, zeros included). Folds: set_artifact_checksum -> set_artifact_checksums (one-item accepts), acknowledge_gap -> acknowledge_gaps, dimension_drift -> dimension_drifts (new optional target_id, dimension), propagate_change -> propagate_from (one ChangeEvent seed reads the change's radius with stale edge prose, seeded_by_change), verifies -> add_verification (id + verifies; a revise keeps omitted fields), graph_report_markdown -> graph_report `format` (json default unchanged, markdown the old document). Retired, nothing replaces them: evidence_report, forecast_readiness, frontier, ility_report, granularity_report, consumption_report, surprising_connections, readiness_report, gate_on (core computations untouched; old handlers kept as <tool>_kept for the December restore). find_tools never offers a stub but weighs words over its unchanged description; draw_edges refuses items naming verifies or gate_on; the remote client forwards set_artifact_checksum unmeasured; writers.json and settles drop the stubs; served text (skills, instructions, VS Code route, connect-time instructions, cues, literals, schema prose, site) names survivors; the first-read cue reads graph_report with format markdown and its id moves from instructions/graph_report_markdown to instructions/graph_report. Reworded, no rename: report_manual_work/manual_work_ledger, add_epoch/plan_epoch, scan_nodes/search_design. Served tools stay 199.
